__models.gap: docs/FORMATS.md §5 'Known gaps' — the four gaps this directory fills
__models.role: The index of every synthetic file. Files whose format cannot carry an inline `__synthetic` marker are listed here instead — see `markerPolicy`.

claudeCodeStamp: CLI 2.1.220 — the corpus these fixtures are shaped against
warning: NOTHING IN THIS DIRECTORY WAS CAPTURED FROM A MACHINE. fixtures/cli/, fixtures/files/ and fixtures/transcripts/ are real output and are the regression baseline (TX.2). fixtures/synthetic/ is constructed, and exists only to exercise behaviour the reference machine cannot witness. Never diff a synthetic fixture against live output; never cite one as evidence of a format.

markerPolicy.inline: Every file whose format tolerates unknown keys carries `__synthetic: true` and `__models` at the top level. That is all the settings-shaped JSON, all the oracles, seed.json, and the three foreign-tool decoy manifests.
markerPolicy.enforced: Check V10 of `generate.mjs verify` asserts that every .json under fixtures/synthetic/ either carries BOTH `__synthetic: true` and `__models`, or matches one of the exemption patterns below. The exemptions are code (generate.mjs → MARKER_EXEMPT), not just prose, so this list cannot quietly grow.
markerPolicy.byIndex: Five kinds of file cannot carry the marker and are identified HERE and in their subtree README instead:

byIndexCases.path: **/.claude-plugin/plugin.json — including all 30 in scale/tree/ and the @skills-dir one
byIndexCases.why: VERIFIED against the live CLI: `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes on the @skills-dir manifest as written, and adding `__synthetic`/`__models` produces two 'Unknown field: … Claude Code ignores it at load time' warnings, which --strict promotes to errors (exit 1). A marker would make these fixtures fail the very gate T1.18 and CI run. They self-identify through name/description/keywords — every generated description begins 'SYNTHETIC FIXTURE —'.
Same manifest-validation exposure as plugin.json. Every entry's description begins 'SYNTHETIC FIXTURE —' and every name is `synthetic-*` / `sy-*`.

A BARE Record<name, entry> at the top level — a `__synthetic` key would read as a marketplace literally named `__synthetic`. Adding it would corrupt the very shape the fixture models. All six entries are named `synthetic-*`.
YAML frontmatter with a fixed key set. Every one says SYNTHETIC FIXTURE in its `description`.

Bare single-value files (a 40-hex SHA, an ISO timestamp) and per-process lock files whose content is a fixed one- or two-key JSON object observed live. No room for a marker without misrepresenting the shape.

markerPolicy.decoysDoCarryMarkers: The four foreign-tool and misplaced manifests under skills-dir-plugin/ (.cursor-plugin/, .codex-plugin/, .kimi-plugin/, and the directory-root plugin.json) DO carry inline markers and are NOT exempt — Claude Code never loads them, so nothing validates them. Their `__models.role` says DECOY.

gaps.gap: No project-scope .claude/settings.json, no local-scope plugin keys, pluginConfigs absent — 4-scope precedence is untestable
openQuestions: Merge granularity (per-key merge vs scope replacement) is UNWITNESSED. The oracle labels every affected assertion MODEL-DEPENDENT and ships entries that discriminate the two models rather than picking one.
The managed-settings file PATH is recorded nowhere in docs/. The fixture is path-agnostic.
pluginConfigs NESTING is inferred from docs/02-architecture.md §4.2, not observed. Its PRECEDENCE RULE is documented (line 158) and is what the fixture really tests.
The canonical id form for a @skills-dir plugin (`<name>@skills-dir`? bare? `@local`?) is NOT invented here — the oracle asserts `origin: "skills-dir"` and leaves the id to T1.6.
